payload.friendly_name: App shell with all its states
payload.purpose_context: Every mission screen in the dashboard and Kitty Desktop sits inside the same frame: top bar, navigation rail and context sidebar. Building that shell first, with all its layouts (picker, project, mission) and its width-driven expanded, collapsed and mobile states, gives later screen missions one consistent, reviewed frame to drop into. Source: issue #2.
payload.purpose_tldr: Build the shared application shell for mission screens, with every layout and width state visible in the workbench.

payload.question: Which window widths separate the expanded, collapsed and mobile tiers?
What does the collapsed tier look like for mission and project screens?
Is the top bar part of the shell, and what does it contain?
Build local pattern elements for layouts sk-app-shell cannot express, or wait for design-library changes?

payload.final_answer: Expanded >= 1100 px, collapsed 620-1099 px, mobile (hamburger drawer) < 620 px
Sidebar shrinks to an icon column; mission screens keep the global rail beside it
Shell owns the top bar: brand, mobile hamburger, slot for host actions; no Settings/Help

Projects picker is outside the shell (no shell, no side rail). Shell has two layouts: project (one sidebar, no rail: Missions, Drift, Ops) and mission (rail + mission sidebar: Pipeline, Work Packages, Artifacts). Where sk-app-shell cannot express a layout, build it locally on sk-* primitives and record the gap for the design library.
